section_1.title: The Core Intuition: The 'Orchestra' Analogy
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that any complex, periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves. Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of periodic functions (sin/cos). Visual: A messy, jagged wave gradually morphs as we add smooth sine waves together.
section_1.example: Imagine a musician playing a chord on a piano; the ear hears one 'complex' sound, but a Fourier Series reveals the individual pure notes (frequencies) that constitute that chord.

section_2.title: The Mathematical Foundation: Basis Functions
section_2.content: Define the Fourier Series formula. Explain the concept of 'orthogonality'—how sine and cosine waves function like independent axes in a space. Visual: A 3D graph showing how multiple simple waves (the building blocks) align to reconstruct a square wave.
section_2.example: Think of this like mixing primary colors (Red, Blue, Yellow) to paint any specific hue in a palette.

section_3.title: Calculating Coefficients: The 'Sieve' Method
section_3.content: Explain how we extract the amplitude of each component using integration. The integral acts as a filter that picks out specific frequencies. Visual: An animation showing a 'sieve' passing over a signal, leaving only the strength of a specific frequency component.
section_3.example: Using a radio tuner: You turn the dial to 'sieve out' one specific station (frequency) from the noisy background of all radio waves in the air.

section_4.title: Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave Demo
section_4.content: Show the progression of adding terms: n=1, n=3, n=10. Discuss the 'Gibbs Phenomenon' (the little overshoot at corners). Visual: A growing stack of sine waves creating sharper and sharper corners of a square wave.
section_4.example: A robotic cat's motion controller: Approximating a sudden jump (square wave) using smooth motor rotations to ensure the mechanical joints don't snap.

section_5.title: Real-World Application & Summary
section_5.content: Summarize how Fourier Series transform time-domain data into frequency-domain data. Final visual: A spectrum analyzer showing real-time bars rising as an audio signal plays.
section_5.example: How your smartphone compresses a high-quality song (MP3) by removing the 'inaudible' frequencies identified via the Fourier process.

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Adding terms creates sharper, more accurate waves.",
            "Convergence improves as we add more terms.",
            "Gibbs phenomenon causes overshoot at signal corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave Demo", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axes for visualization
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-PI, PI], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Target Square Wave
        square_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if x > 0 else -1, color=WHITE)
        
        # Initial state: Show square wave outline
        self.add(square_wave)
        
        # Function to generate Fourier sum
        def fourier_sum(n_terms):
            def func(x):
                res = 0
                for i in range(n_terms):
                    n = 2 * i + 1
                    res += (4 / (np.pi * n)) * np.sin(n * x)
                return res
            return func

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Adding terms creates sharper, more accurate waves.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        f1 = axes.plot(fourier_sum(1), color="#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(f1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Convergence improves as we add more terms.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        f10 = axes.plot(fourier_sum(10), color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(Transform(f1, f10))
        
        # Error bar
        error_bar = Line(start=axes.c2p(2, 0), end=axes.c2p(2, 0.5), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(error_bar))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Gibbs phenomenon causes overshoot at signal corners.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Show overshoot zoom/highlight
        overshoot = Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 1.2))
        self.play(Create(overshoot))
        self.wait(2)
